summary: Concurrent deferred-retry causes reordered function calls when orchestrating long-running tasks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer runs an orchestration service that coordinates multi-step tool/function calls using Redwood Python SDK for generation + external webhooks to execute side effects. When multiple user sessions overlap, background retry/coalescing logic in the orchestrator defers retries and batches them, which appears to reorder external function invocations across sessions.

Impact:
- Customer observed out-of-order side effects (payment capture before customer-notify) across different sessions for ~0.2% of requests during peak traffic, causing transactional integrity issues.
- Affects production flows for several customers using NimbleDocs' document-processing pipeline; user-facing errors and manual reconciliation required.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated, prod us-east region
- NimbleDocs orchestration service (Go and TS microservices), primary call site uses python-sdk v1.6.2 for generation and function-calling
- External webhook endpoints run behind company API gateway with per-tenant routing

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Kick off two long-running sessions (Session A and Session B) that each call the model which then issues a sequence of tool calls: notify_user -> reserve_funds -> capture_funds -> final_ack.
2) During peak load, artificially induce a transient 503 from the webhook for reserve_funds for Session A (to trigger retry).
3) Orchestrator defers and coalesces retries into a short retry window; Session B proceeds normally.
4) Observe captured side effects: in ~1 of 500 runs, capture_funds for Session B executes before notify_user for Session A.

Expected behavior:
- Retries for a given session should preserve the original relative order of function/tool invocations for that session and should not allow interleaving that violates per-session transactional ordering.

Actual behavior:
- Deferred/coalesced retries in the orchestration layer can be executed out-of-order relative to other sessions, and our telemetry shows occasional interleaving across sessions that results in inconsistent external side effects.

Logs / artifacts provided by customer (sanitized):
- Snippets of webhook timestamps and ids (session-scoped ids preserved).
- Orchestrator trace ids: trace-nyc-2134, trace-nyc-2139 (attached in ticket).
- SDK request logs show identical idempotency-key patterns reused at the session level, but the orchestrator's internal retry-queue assigns a separate execution batch id.

Temporary workaround requested:
- Customer asks for guidance to force per-session strict ordering until we identify root cause.
- Suggested workaround sought: SDK-level per-call confirmation tokens or a recommended idempotency scoping pattern to guarantee at-most-once per-session ordering.
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Aisha Mehta (Customer): We attempted to reproduce in staging with synthetic 503s and saw the same interleaving at a much lower rate. We can share sanitized logs and a small harness to reproduce.

2026-03-01 12:03 - Michael Chen (Support): Thanks Aisha — assigning eng to investigate. Can you attach the sanitized orchestrator trace and the set of idempotency keys you used? Also confirm python-sdk version.

2026-03-01 15:47 - Aisha Mehta (Customer): Attached traces trace-nyc-2134/2139 and a small script that simulates two sessions (link to harness). Using python-sdk v1.6.2. Webhook gateway injects a 503 for reserve_funds for session A.

2026-03-02 08:10 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Initial hypothesis: orchestrator's retry-coalescer batches deferred retries and assigns a global batch priority; execution order uses batch FIFO but mixes outputs from different sessions. This could interleave per-session calls if the orchestrator doesn't re-assert session sequencing when dequeuing. Seeing related race in internal queue metrics (queue-shard-7).

2026-03-03 10:34 - Michael Chen (Support): Quick mitigation suggestion provided to customer: switch to per-call idempotency keys scoped at action-level (sessionId:actionSeq) and enable explicit ordering by awaiting confirmation before emitting the next call. Provided code example for python and ts to serialize calls.

2026-03-04 11:20 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally with orchestration harness. Root cause narrowed: orchestrator coalescer emits a batch token and uses parallel worker pool to execute batch items; workers fetch next available item without re-checking session ordinal. When a deferred item for session A re-enters the pool, it may be executed after a later live item from session B. Suggested fix: include per-session sequence barrier when scheduling deferred retries or tag batch items with session-order and enforce per-session worker affinity during drain.

2026-03-05 09:05 - Michael Chen (Support): Noted follow-up action: Eng will push a small change to orchestrator to enforce per-session ordering in the deferred-retry drain path; releasing a hotfix to staging for testing. Also documenting recommended SDK pattern for idempotency scoping (sessionId:actionSeq) as short-term guidance.
investigation_notes: Orchestrator retry-coalescer uses global batching window (50ms) to reduce webhook fanout. Batches are stored in queue-shard-* and drained by N workers.
Workers take items from the same shard without session affinity; sessions with deferred retries can be drained interleaved with live items from other sessions.
Python SDK usage: customer uses session-level idempotency keys rather than per-action keys; combined with orchestrator batching this increases chance of cross-session interleaving of side effects.
Telemetry: ~0.2% occurrence at peak traffic; correlates with batch window hit rate > 12% and worker pool size > 8.
resolution: In progress: engineering implemented a patch to add session-affinity barriers when draining deferred retry batches. Hotfix deployed to staging 2026-03-05 for validation. Short-term customer guidance provided: use per-action idempotency keys (format sessionId:seq) and await explicit acknowledgement before issuing dependent calls. Planned follow-ups: monitor staging for 72h, roll to prod if no regressions, and publish SDK best-practice note to Confluence.
next_steps: Validate hotfix in staging with customer's harness (priority).
If staging looks good, schedule prod rollout in a low-traffic window with canary (10%).
Author KB article showing per-action idempotency pattern with code snippets for python/ts/go.
Postmortem if fix does not fully eliminate interleaving (assign Sev1 incident process).
